name: VA-10

key_factors: Prediction markets price Subramanyam at 94-96% to win
Subramanyam holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge with outside support and no opposition spending

model.rationale: Prediction markets put Subramanyam's chances at 94-96%, his fundraising dwarfs the challenger's, and the district's Democratic lean plus incumbent advantages all point the same direction. With no polling to confirm the gap, the margin is set modestly below what fundamentals alone would suggest and uncertainty stays wide.
model.watch: Any late independent polling or Republican outside spending showing Subramanyam below the mid-50s would signal a tighter race than markets currently price.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Suhas Subramanyam, a first-term Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a northern Virginia district that leans Democratic by about six points. He faces Republican Dave Beckwith, who has raised roughly $107,000, along with a minor independent candidate. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

The financial picture is lopsided: Subramanyam has raised about $1.17 million with $583,000 on hand and backing from outside groups, while no opposition spending has been recorded against him. Prediction markets put his chances at roughly 94 to 96 percent. With the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's money advantage, and market pricing all aligned, the seat is expected to remain Democratic, though the lack of polling leaves some room for doubt.
